title: Router only response first route if using dependency injection on router
body:
This is related to #4528 

Full codes are as per following:

<details>
<summary>/index.js</summary>

```js
const express = require('express');
const app = express();

app.use('/buy',require('./routes/buy'))
app.use('/sell',require('./routes/sell'))

app.listen(5000,()=>{
  console.log('Server start')
})
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>/routes/buy.js</summary>

```js
const express = require('express')
const router = express.Router()
const buyController = require('../controller/buy.js')

router.use('/:id/log', require('./log')(router, 'BuyModel'))
router.route('/').get(buyController.fetchBuys)

module.exports = router
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>/routes/sell.js</summary>

```js
const express = require('express')
const router = express.Router()

router.use('/:id/log', require('./log')(router, 'SaleModel'))

module.exports = router
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>/routes/log.js</summary>

```js
const logController = require('../controller/log')

module.exports = function(router, model){
  router.route('/')
    .get(logController.fetchLogs(model))
  return router
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>/controller/log.js</summary>

```js
exports.fetchLogs = model => (req, res, next) => {
  console.log('fetch logs');
  console.log('base_url:', req.baseUrl);
  console.log('...');

  return res.status(200).send('done')
}
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>/controller/buy.js</summary>

```js
exports.fetchBuys = (req, res, next) => {
  console.log('base_url:', req.baseUrl);
  console.log('result: fetch buys');
  console.log('...')
  res.status(200).send()
}

```
</details>

---

Current code consoles:

**GET: /buy**
fetch logs
base_url: /buy

**GET: /buy/123/log**
fetch logs
base_url: /buy/123/log

---

What I hope is:

**GET: /buy**
fetch buys
base_url: /buy

**GET: /buy/123/log**
fetch logs
base_url: /buy/123/log

---

If I reverse the route sequence in /routes/buy.js like following

```js
router.route('/').get(buyController.fetchBuys)
router.use('/:id/log', require('./log')(router, 'BuyModel'))
```

**GET: /buy**
fetch buys
base_url: /buy

**GET: /buy/123/log**
fetch buys
base_url: /buy/123/log

---

Would like to know how can I make it work if I still want to use dependency injection in router
author: orzinc

comments.body:
The issue is that in your `/routes/log.js` file, it has a function that accepts a `router` and attaches the fetchLogs to the GET / route on that router. Of course, you are passing the router that belongs to the buys route in `/routes/buy.js`, so the GET / ends up pointing there. The reason it changes when you arrange lines is because you changed which of the two GET / you have on the same router.

There are two ways to fix this:

1. Change line 5 in `/routes/buy.js` to `router.use('/:id/log', require('./log')(express.Router(), 'BuyModel'))`
2. Change line 5 in `/routes/buy.js` to `router.use(require('./log')(router, 'BuyModel'))` and then change line 4 in `/routes/log.js` to `router.route('/:id/log')` (and of course change line 4 in `/routes/sell.js` to the `app.use` as well.

I hope this helps!
@dougwilson Thank you for your help, and it works great 👍

satisfaction_conditions: A solution that prevents route handler conflicts when using dependency injection in Express routers
An approach that maintains the ability to use dependency injection for passing model information to routes
A fix that ensures routes respond with the correct handler based on the URL path
An explanation of why the current implementation causes the routing problem

title: trust-proxy function not called?
author: Ionaru

comments.body:
Hi @Ionaru . The trust proxy function is called when trust of addresses needs to be established. In your example, there is no code that needs to know anything about the upstream, so for optimization reasons, it will not get invoked.

If you add something like `req.ip`, `req.hostname` etc to your example, your function should then get called, as Express tries to determine the address.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of when the trust-proxy function gets called
Clarification on the optimization behavior of Express regarding proxy trust
Practical examples of when the trust proxy function would be triggered

title: IP address as a url param error
body:
When declaring an IP address as a URL parameter `req.params` incorrectly parses the value. 

Add the following param to the URL  `:ip((?:[0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3})`

Use the value 192.168.1.2 for ip

Then check  `req.params.ip` it will return as 1. 

```
console.log('req.originalUrl',req.originalUrl);
console.log('(req.params.ip',req.params.ip);
```
author: DaleCox

comments.body:
Hi, Can you supply a full app that reproduces the error (as there are many things that can influence this?

Also, it may just be because your param definition does not work with `path-to-regexp` module. Try using `:ip([0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3})`

Unfortunately I don't have anything I can post at this time. 

Thank you the reg ex you provided solved the issue.
Gotcha. If the updated reg ex worked, then it looks like it's just a limitation in `path-to-regexp` that we use, which is what I thought (you cannot use `(?:` in the reg ex).

satisfaction_conditions: A working regular expression pattern for capturing IP addresses in URL parameters
A solution that addresses the limitation in path-to-regexp module's parsing of IP addresses
A pattern that correctly captures all four octets of an IP address in URL parameters
